pairs.subject: error-handling
pairs.evidence: lib/notebook/corpus.ts:102 The corpus gate groups and snapshots refusals by rule keys it builds from message text with regexes (`ruleOf`), even though graph findings had a typed `GraphIssueKind` when they were created. Rewording any rule therefore changes approved verdicts, and one cause can split across several wordings.

techniques.evidence: lib/notebook/graph.ts:72 The typed `GraphIssue.kind` from cards.ts is written into the prose `rule` and never kept as a field. This is the 'failures the system mints itself' loss the technique names.

lib/notebook/corpus.ts:55 `NotebookFinding` carries `path`/`rule`/`observed` but no rule id. Its one branching consumer (the corpus probe and gate) has to recover the kind, and shape-rule identity, by matching prose.
lib/notebook/failure.ts:18 A model answer is one document, so it is refused whole and every finding names its position as a JSON path. The draft is kept for repair.

lib/notebook/corpus.ts:100 The catch is narrow: only the expected refusal becomes a verdict, and anything else is rethrown. Minor: `sameAddress` in retrieval.ts:150 uses a bare `catch {}` for URL normalisation without saying it drops the error on purpose.
lib/notebook/shape.ts:162 A caught compile failure becomes a path-addressed finding that reaches the refusal, not a silent skip.

pairs.subject: error-handling
pairs.evidence: packages/domain/src/door.ts:52 The schema door keeps only the first zod issue and writes its field path into the message string. `detail` holds the door name, not the field. The forms that errors.ts says 'show field-level detail' can only get the failing field by parsing prose, and all other issues are lost.

techniques.evidence: packages/domain/src/door.ts:68 The validation failure's category-specific data (the field and the other issues) is stringified at the boundary. Only issues[0] survives, as prose.

packages/domain/src/errors.ts:20 `internal` is both the impossible class and the catch-all. That gives up the zero-rate detector the technique relies on: any unrecognised foreign failure lands in `internal` too.
packages/domain/src/errors.ts:2 Closed union of 8 codes, each justified by the consumer that branches on it. Transience is stated only in comments, not as data, and there is no retry-interval field.
packages/domain/src/errors.ts:85 The external HTTP code is an exhaustive Record keyed by the taxonomy, beside its declaration. A new code without a status does not compile.
packages/domain/src/errors.ts:63 The published package hands out a closed, branchable code (with an `isAppError` brand that works across module copies), not an opaque aggregate.
packages/domain/src/door.ts:82 The only JSON.parse catch turns into a classified Result and keeps `cause`.

pairs.subject: error-handling
pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/library/_port/handoff.ts:16 When the kernel store cannot be opened, the style handoff passes the id through and reaches no door. A store outage then shows up downstream as the atelier's 404, and nobody is told the store was down.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/library/_port/handoff.ts:16 A fallback with no telemetry or log is 'an outage with good manners'.
app/(studio)/library/_port/handoff.ts:17 Every `readStyle` failure code (unavailable or internal, not only not-found) is collapsed to 'try the next candidate' and dropped without being declared.
app/(studio)/library/_port/real.ts:196 Re-wrapped without `{ cause: e }`, so the original FoundryError and its status are lost. Unmapped statuses (e.g. 500/502) fall into `internal`.
app/(studio)/library/_port/real.ts:129 A foreign failure is classified on its structured status in one table, not on its message.
app/(studio)/library/_port/real.ts:47 Each side answers the domain's closed `Result`, which actions.ts turns into the wire envelope for the client island.

app/(studio)/library/_port/real.ts:178 The kernel's 'nothing changed' becomes a conflict worded the same way as fixture.ts:198/204, so the failure reads the same on both sides. There is no shared registry or suggested-action field.
